record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README calls this a replication of Arditi et al. and reports held-out results applying a difference-in-means direction and ablation/addition interventions.
record.gate_note: The README reports held-out refusal results, control-vector comparisons, and collateral-effect checks. It also mentions a layer-sweep figure, but the plotted values are not available in the text. Method settings and hyperparameters used for selection are not recorded as result rows.
record.test_reason: A self-described replication of Arditi et al. on Qwen3-4B. It uses the same difference-in-means direction, the same projection ablation and vector addition, and refusal rates on held-out prompts, with random and contrast-direction controls.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The author concludes that one difference-in-means direction mediates refusal in Qwen3-4B in both directions (necessity and sufficiency), with intervals separated from both controls. They report no collateral damage on their checks and say the direction is specific to harmful prompts. They flag one model, the harm/topic confound and an unmatched contrast control as limitations, with Qwen3-8B replication as the main open item.
record.recipe_differences: The README describes this as a replication of Arditi et al. using Qwen3-4B and the difference in mean harmful and harmless activations, with projection ablation and vector addition. It uses its own held-out prompt setup, controls, and validated LLM judge; the repository contains code and result files, but the code was not read or run.
record.method_sensitivity: The README says the effect is confined to layers 20–23. The reported direction is read from layer 21 of 36 at the post-instruction token. The README also notes that the KL threshold and 0.8·L cutoff were taken from the paper rather than calibrated here.

fits_no_version.finding: The direction is built from AdvBench/TDC/HarmBench and tested mostly on JailbreakBench, and the test numbers hold across these sources.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The refusal direction generalises across harmful-prompt datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating r removes 15.3% of the squared activation norm on harmful prompts versus 0.25% on harmless ones. Random directions remove about 0.01% and the contrast direction 0.8%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The refusal direction carries a large, harm-specific share of activation norm.

record.problems: Only one model is reported; the README says val uses 32 harmful prompts and one data seed. It notes harmfulness is confounded with topic, the contrast control is not matched on removal magnitude, and 21/1088 test rows could not be judged and count as non-refusal. It also says the KL threshold and 0.8·L cutoff are taken from the paper rather than calibrated here. The layer-sweep results are presented as a figure, without numerical values in the README.
record.rows_left_out: No plotted values from conditions.png or layers.png are transcribed. The README reports no separate numerical KL values from the layer sweep.

untested.parts: Preservation of broad general capabilities (benchmarks such as MMLU), beyond harmless-prompt compliance and an incoherence count. Only one model (Qwen3-4B).
No jailbreak mechanism or adversarial training.
No multi-direction, cone or affine analysis.
Harm/topic confound is acknowledged, but no separate harmfulness measure.
Only prompt-source transfer; no language, model-variant or base-to-instruct transfer.
No comparison of training methods or stages.
Qwen3 thinking mode is not examined; no reasoning-model analysis reported.

missing.what: Addition at α=4 makes outputs 100% incoherent (a dose limit on the addition result).
missing.locator: README, 'Three things that would have produced a wrong answer'

missing.what: The α value used for the reported 98% addition result.
Per-layer refusal and KL values from the sweep.
Qwen3-0.6B and 1.7B refuse about 0/32 and 7/32 harmful prompts at baseline, so V1 could not be tested on them.
An early selected direction had KL = 15 on harmless prompts and broke the model.
missing.locator: README, 'Three things that would have produced a wrong answer'

record.verdict_notes: I removed R10 from the reader's limits_scope label. 1/1088 incoherent supports capability preservation, and the lack of broad capability tests is untested, not limiting. R12–R14 are diagnostics and are now unlinked. The source is a README only, with unpeered code, so results are self-reported.

versions.untested_parts: The README reports harmless-prompt compliance and an incoherence count, but does not establish preservation of broad general capability beyond those checks.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration result is reported.
No jailbreak attack mechanism or training against ablation is tested.
The contrast-direction control is compared with the refusal direction, but the README does not test an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account of refusal.
No separate harmfulness judgment measure is reported.
No language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test is reported.
No comparison of refusal training methods or training stages is reported.

relation.reason: Reports its own ablation and addition refusal rates with controls on Qwen3-4B.

tranche.reason: Self-described replication of Arditi et al. Uses the same difference-in-means direction at post-instruction positions, projection at every writer, one-layer addition, refusal rate on held-out (mostly JailbreakBench) prompts. Only the judge differs (LLM judge, kappa=0.93).

source_check.notes: The text is the top-level README only. The experiment README (full method), the alpha behind the 98% result and the per-layer sweep values are not in it. Qwen3-4B's thinking mode is not stated. 21/1088 test rows were unjudged and counted as non-refusal.

statements.correction: gh:danorel reports collateral-damage checks: 64/64 harmless compliance under r ablation; 1/1088 test rows judged incoherent; a KL guard on harmless prompts in the layer sweep. No benchmark scores. Addition contrast control: 2% [0–8].
statements.problem: Every number and condition for gh:danorel is right (86%->5% vs 88% random/88% contrast; 0%->98% vs 0% random; n=64; layer 21 of 36, post-instruction token; all-writer projection; Wilson CIs; one model). But the 'why' line credits capability checks to the other three studies and leaves out gh:danorel, which the record marks capability=y.
